flows.narrative: Despite the week's brutal price action (S&P down five straight sessions into Friday's sharpest single-day move), BOTH BofA/EPFR and Lipper's newly-published week-ended-18-Nov editions show net equity INFLOWS, not capitulation outflows -- a genuinely counterintuitive result this run flags rather than forces into the price/sentiment narrative. BofA/EPFR: global equity funds +$66.6bn, US equities +$45.6bn (7th straight week), tech funds +$5.4bn (8th straight week), EM equities +$8.3bn (8th straight week); bonds -$7.4bn (first outflow since April 2025) and EM debt -$7.5bn (most since April 2020); crypto funds -$1.1bn; BofA's own Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 7.1 from 7.4 (re-confirmed this run via an independent Yahoo Finance writeup of the same Hartnett note -- money-market +$0.4bn and gold +$0.2bn both matched exactly, cross-validating Saturday's bake rather than contradicting it). Lipper: US equity funds +$45.71bn (largest since 23 Sep, 3rd straight week), tech funds +$10.3bn (largest since 16 Jun), global equity funds +$59.23bn (9th straight week); US bond funds -$5.58bn (first outflow in 4 weeks, high-yield -$2.31bn, long Treasury -$2.64bn); money market -$19.12bn (2nd straight weekly outflow). ICI has not yet published a week-ended-18-Nov edition (still on week ended 11 Nov). Two leads chased this run for the still-missing Europe/China/Japan/Gold standalone breakouts both turned out inapplicable and were discarded rather than used: an isimarkets EPFR chartbook (dated week ending 19 Nov *2025*, wrong year) and a globalbankingandfinance Europe-inflow writeup (week ended 11 Nov 2026, the wrong week). This run fills two gaps flagged Sunday as unconfirmed: BofA/EPFR data shows a Japan equity-fund outflow of -$4.2bn (the biggest since May 2026) and a Gold-fund inflow of just +$0.2bn -- negligible, and notably NOT safe-haven behavior, since spot gold fell roughly 8.7% the same week alongside equities and crypto in what reads as broad margin-driven deleveraging rather than a flight to havens. A China-specific figure still cannot be cleanly isolated from EPFR/BofA; the closest available is Lipper's broader Asia-ex-Japan fund category (-$2.78bn), reported here as an explicit proxy, not a China-only number.
